questions.q: In a database, which type of key is used to uniquely identify each row?
questions.e: A primary key uniquely identifies each row in a table.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of NoSQL databases over relational databases?
questions.e: NoSQL databases scale out easily and handle flexible, changing data. Relational databases enforce a strict structure.

questions.q: What is the purpose of normalization in databases?
o: To reduce data redundancy and improve consistency
questions.e: Normalisation splits data into related tables to reduce repeated data and keep it consistent.

questions.q: Which of the following is a property of transactions in databases?
questions.e: ACID is the set of properties of database transactions.

questions.q: What is the purpose of normalization in a database?
questions.e: Normalisation reduces redundancy (repeated data).

questions.q: What does the "HAVING" clause do in SQL?
questions.e: HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY. WHERE filters rows before grouping.

questions.q: Which of the following is true about primary and foreign keys?
o: Foreign keys create relationships between tables
Primary keys can have NULL values
questions.e: A foreign key links a row to the primary key of another table.

questions.q: What type of NoSQL database is MongoDB?
questions.e: MongoDB stores JSON-like documents, so it is a document database.

questions.q: What does the term "indexing" mean in a database?
o: Sorting data to improve query performance
Creating unique constraints on a column
questions.e: An index is a sorted lookup structure that makes queries faster.

questions.q: Which SQL keyword is used to remove duplicate records in a query result?
questions.e: DISTINCT removes duplicate rows from a result.

questions.q: What is a materialized view in a database?
o: A dynamically updated view of a query
A physical copy of query results stored for future use
questions.e: A materialised view stores the result of a query physically so it can be read quickly.

questions.q: What is the difference between OLTP and OLAP systems?
o: OLTP focuses on transaction processing, OLAP on data analysis
OLAP processes transactions, OLTP processes queries
OLAP uses SQL, OLTP uses NoSQL
Both are identical systems with different interfaces
questions.e: OLTP handles day-to-day transactions. OLAP is for analysing large amounts of data.

questions.q: Which SQL command is used to add a new column to an existing table?
questions.e: ALTER TABLE changes a table's structure, for example ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN c.

questions.q: Which of the following is used to define a relationship between two tables in SQL?
questions.e: A JOIN combines rows from two tables using a related column.

questions.q: What is the default sorting order of the ORDER BY clause in SQL?
questions.e: ORDER BY sorts in ascending order by default.

questions.q: What is the role of a database view?
o: A log for storing SQL queries
A stored procedure for querying data
A virtual table representing a query result
questions.e: A view is a virtual table made from a stored query.

questions.q: Which of the following SQL constraints ensures that all values in a column are unique?
questions.e: UNIQUE makes sure no two rows have the same value in that column.

questions.q: Which SQL statement is used to delete a table and its data permanently?
questions.e: DROP TABLE deletes the table and its data. TRUNCATE empties the rows but keeps the table, and DELETE removes rows.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a cloud-based database?
questions.e: Amazon RDS is a database service that runs in the cloud.

questions.q: In the MVC (Model-View-Controller) pattern, where is the business logic typically implemented?
questions.e: In MVC the Model holds the data and the business logic.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a key component of the Hadoop ecosystem?
questions.e: Hadoop includes HDFS, YARN and MapReduce. SQL is a query language, not a Hadoop component.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of using NoSQL databases for big data?
o: Ability to handle unstructured and semi-structured data
questions.e: NoSQL databases handle unstructured and semi-structured big data well.

questions.q: In database terminology, what does "SQL" stand for?
questions.e: SQL stands for Structured Query Language.

questions.q: In the context of databases, what does the term "index" refer to?
o: A unique identifier for a database
The primary key of a table
A data structure that improves the speed of data retrieval operations on a database table
questions.e: An index speeds up data retrieval from a table.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of the SQL SELECT statement in a database?
questions.e: SELECT retrieves data.

questions.q: What does the term "Big Data" refer to?
o: A specific type of file format
Datasets that are too large to be processed by traditional databases
questions.e: Big data is too large or complex for traditional databases.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of using a NoSQL database over a relational database?
o: Ability to handle large amounts of unstructured data
questions.e: NoSQL databases handle large amounts of unstructured data.

questions.q: Which database model uses a table-based structure with rows and columns?
questions.e: A relational database stores data in tables of rows and columns.

questions.q: In the context of databases, what does SQL stand for?
questions.e: SQL stands for Structured Query Language.

questions.q: Multics provided the first commercial relational database product, the Multics Relational Data Store (MRDS). In which year?
questions.e: The Multics Relational Data Store, in 1978, was the first commercial relational database.
